external_primary_research.finding: WIT resource types are indirect handles; owned handles transfer unique ownership while borrow<T> is a temporary loan.
Component Model resource handle uniqueness/drop rules are dynamically enforced; resource types are generative per component instance.
Async borrow correctness uses runtime num_lends/num_borrows bookkeeping and traps invalid drop/return transitions.
Scala capture checking tracks capabilities in capture sets and can express resource/effect constraints statically; current system remains experimental.
Capability classifiers extend Scala capture checking with semantic capability categories and mechanized effect-safety results.
Revocable capabilities demonstrate flow-sensitive typestate that can provide, revoke and return capabilities rather than tying all lifetimes to lexical scope.

hypotheses.claim: Lexical/scope-only capability validity is insufficient for self.root effects that cross asynchronous task, restart, resource-epoch or lease boundaries.
hypotheses.strongest_counterhypothesis: A sufficiently expressive static capture/typestate system can encode every relevant lifecycle fact, making residual runtime currentness checks unnecessary.
hypotheses.falsifier: Show a static ClayCode contract that rejects stale/revoked/reconstructed bearer use and accepts legitimate rebind/renewal across target-VPS restart/lease transitions without consulting dynamic currentness evidence.

hypotheses.claim: Rigid raw epoch equality is safer than scope-only validity but can falsely deny legitimate resource rebind/lease renewal; an exact provenance-bound revalidation receipt can preserve fail-closed currentness without treating stale identity as current.
hypotheses.strongest_counterhypothesis: Always rejecting any epoch/lease mismatch is operationally acceptable and simpler; revalidation receipts add forgery/state complexity without useful reduction in false denial.
hypotheses.falsifier: On real target-VPS lifecycle fixtures, compare rigid epoch rejection with receipt-bound revalidation for safety, false denial, replay/restart behavior and resource cost.

out_of_box_experiment.interpretation: Within this deliberately constructed mechanism model, scope-only validation cannot distinguish stale/revoked/reconstructed authority, while rigid exact-epoch validation rejects positively revalidated rebinding/renewal. Receipt-aware currentness separates both classes. Because the ground-truth model itself encodes these lifecycle distinctions, this experiment is a discriminating architecture sanity check, not empirical evidence of real-world rates or a production proof.

fusion.supported_direction: Keep WP03 nominal semantic/resource/capability identity separate from runtime bearer/currentness identity; let WP04 and runtime enforce dynamic scope/freshness/revocation. Do not mint bearer authority from serialized descriptors.
fusion.new_refinement: When a resource/lease epoch legitimately changes, accept continuity only through a verified revalidation/renewal receipt bound to the intended semantic contract/resource identity; never by descriptive equality or stale payload reuse.
fusion.reason: Existing Epoch/Ref/Receipt/capability/effect primitives appear sufficient to express the test obligation.

architecture_delta.proposed_change: Add an executable authority-lifetime differential that distinguishes scope validity, stale/revoked/reconstructed bearer state, rigid epoch mismatch and positively receipt-revalidated rebind/renewal. If implementation needs revalidation, bind the receipt to semantic contract/resource identity plus old/new epoch/lease identities and verification provenance.
architecture_delta.strongest_counterhypothesis: Rigid mismatch rejection dominates once real false-denial cost and attack surface are measured.
architecture_delta.rollback: No production source, frozen semantics, package status or Harness authority was changed by this run. Reject the candidate if target-VPS differential evidence does not show net benefit.
